description: One cup of butter weighs 226 grams and one stick weighs 113 grams. Convert butter between cups, grams, sticks, and tablespoons, with the table.

examples.result: 3/4 cup of butter = about 170 g (1 1/2 sticks).
steps: Multiply by the weight of one cup: 0.75 × 226 g.
examples.title: 3/4 cup of butter to grams

examples.result: 250 g of butter = just over 1 cup, about 2 sticks and 1 1/2 tablespoons.
steps: Divide by the weight of one cup: 250 ÷ 226.
examples.title: 250 g of butter to cups

faqs.answer: 226 grams. A cup of butter is two US sticks, and each stick weighs 113 grams.
faqs.question: How many grams are in a cup of butter?

faqs.answer: 113 grams. One stick is half a cup, or 8 tablespoons.
faqs.question: How many grams is one stick of butter?

faqs.answer: 16 tablespoons. One stick is 8 tablespoons, and a cup is two sticks.
faqs.question: How many tablespoons are in a cup of butter?

faqs.answer: A cup of melted butter weighs slightly more than a cup of firm butter, because melting removes the air. Measure butter firm, then melt it, unless the recipe says to measure it melted.
faqs.question: Does melted butter weigh the same as firm butter?

faqs.answer: Yes, by weight. A 250-gram block of European butter is just over a cup. Do not rely on stick marks. European butter does not come in US sticks, so weigh it.
faqs.question: Can I use European butter in a US recipe?

felicityNote: The tablespoon marks on the wrapper are the best free tool in baking. I still weigh it for pastry, but for everything else the marks are close enough.

parts.meaning: The volume in the recipe, measured firm and levelled.
The grams in one cup of butter, two sticks of 113 grams each.
The grams in one US stick of butter (1/2 cup, 8 tablespoons).

formula.text: Grams = cups × 226. Cups = grams ÷ 226. Sticks = grams ÷ 113.

howToSteps.name: Read the wrapper
howToSteps.text: A US stick of butter has tablespoon marks printed on the wrapper. One stick is 8 tablespoons, half a cup, 113 grams.

howToSteps.name: Cut what you need
howToSteps.text: Cut the stick at the mark for the tablespoons the recipe calls for. For cups, remember two sticks make a cup.

howToSteps.name: Measure firm
howToSteps.text: Measure butter firm from the fridge, not softened or melted, unless the recipe says otherwise. Soft butter packs differently and the cup weight changes.

howToSteps.name: Convert or weigh
howToSteps.text: One cup is 226 grams, one stick is 113 grams, one tablespoon is about 14 grams. Use the converter above for anything in between.

name: Butter
sourceNote: King Arthur Baking lists butter at 113 g per 1/2 cup (1 stick), so 1 cup is 226 g.
title: Cups to Grams: Butter (and Sticks)
tutorial: Butter is the one ingredient where the cup and the stick agree. One US stick of butter is half a cup, 8 tablespoons, and 113 grams. Two sticks make a cup: 226 grams. The wrapper even has tablespoon marks printed on it, which is the closest thing to a free measuring tool in the kitchen.

The number comes from King Arthur Baking's chart: 113 grams per half cup. Double it and a cup is 226 grams. Some charts round that to 227 grams, which is the weight of a cup of water. Close enough that it never matters in a recipe, but 226 is the number the stick math gives you.

Measure butter firm, not melted, when a recipe calls for cups. Melted butter settles differently and a cup of melted butter is not the same as a cup of firm butter. If the recipe wants melted butter, melt it after measuring. The sticks make this easy: cut what you need, then melt it.

The converter works in every direction: cups to grams, grams to cups, and sticks to either. A recipe that calls for 170 grams of butter is 1 1/2 sticks, three quarters of a cup. A recipe that calls for 3 tablespoons is 42 grams, just under half a stick.

European butter is the one thing to watch. It comes in 250-gram blocks, not 113-gram sticks, and it has slightly less water in it. The cup weight is near enough the same, but do not count on the stick marks. Weigh it instead.
